newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa flounders at lows after origin hedges.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa flounders at lows after origin hedges.

text.p: Cocoa futures managed to hold above support despite overhead pressure from origin pre-hedging moves but the March contract failed to muster enough upside momentum to attempt the 900 stg barrier.
"Origins are in the market and people are pre-hedging right from the start," said one trader.
"But it's been fairly quiet, all the volume has been on the near March -- this pre-hedging seems to happen every day."
Traders said the fourth quarter Dutch cocoa grind figure -- a rise of 3.90 percent over the same period in 1995 -- was broadly in line with expectations.
Market prices were unlikely to show any sharp movements unless the U.K. and German grind data, expected later this week, were sharply different to expectations, they said.
"Unless something drastic happens with the U.K. and German (grinds) I don't think it'll have an effect," the trader said.
At the midday break the benchmark March contract stood six stg lower at 889 after sinking to an intraday low of 888 stg. Light buying interest from manufacturers was noted to keep values propped up.
All other positions lost ground in an overall volume of 1,940 lots and were hovering around session lows by the break.
Technical analysts said if March were to show more strength than of late it would be hard-pressed to break through a swathe of resistance reaching into a heavy supply area around 940 stg.

Resistance is also expected to come from a cluster of short-term moving averages stretching up to the 40-day line at 920 stg, although the 10-day average should act as the initial barrier at 898 stg, just above Monday's high.
